title: Differentiation
objectives: Definition of Derivative, its Meaning and Geometrical Interpretation
Derivatives of Exponential, Logarithmic, Parametric and Implicit
summary: As this unit transitions from the study of limits (previous unit) to the derivative, this unit begins by defining it fundamentally as the instantaneous rate of change and geometrically as the slope of the tangent line to a curve at a given point. It introduces the First Principle of Derivatives—the formal limit-based method for finding a derivative—before moving on to efficient differentiation techniques like the Chain Rule for composite functions.

High-Impact Wrap-Up

As this unit transitions from the study of limits (previous unit) to the derivative, this unit begins by defining it fundamentally as the instantaneous rate of change and geometrically as the slope of the tangent line to a curve at a given point. It introduces the First Principle of Derivatives—the formal limit-based method for finding a derivative—before moving on to efficient differentiation techniques like the Chain Rule for composite functions.
